summary: Launch readiness: election coverage lifecycle (active — CA depth, automation, ingestion strategy), multi-state portability (CA+TX done), election+school onboarding (done), representative lookup (done), turnkey onboarding (done), federation queries, billing, operator tooling, multi-scale participation (done)

multi_state_portability.description: Abstract election data infrastructure for multi-state support. Enable individual contributors to add new states by implementing a clear interface. Priority: all-CA coverage + top 5 states (TX, FL, NY, PA, IL).

items.name: state_election_config
items.description: Create StateElectionConfig frozen dataclass capturing per-state election rules (primary month, deadline offsets, governor cycle, senate stagger, statewide offices, chamber names). Populate CA config from current hardcoded values. Refactor cycles.py to use config instead of hardcoded CA constants. Keep backward-compatible wrappers.
items.notes: Phase 1 of multi-state plan. cycles.py already has state='CA' param on get_next_election_date() but ignores it. Extract CA_SENATE_CLASSES, governor base year 2026, senate stagger, statewide offices into config. ~1 session.

items.name: deadline_generalization
items.description: Generalize deadlines.py from CA-only to config-driven. Create generate_deadlines(election_date, state_code) that reads offsets from StateElectionConfig. Keep generate_ca_deadlines() as backward-compatible wrapper.
items.notes: Phase 2. Can combine with Phase 1 or 3. Current CA offsets: registration=15d, VBM=29d, early_voting=10d, conditional_registration=election_day. ~0.5 session.

items.name: state_election_provider
items.description: Create StateElectionProvider ABC with detect_election_sources() and default deadline/cycle methods. Extract CA logic from onboard.py:detect_election_sources() into providers/california.py. Refactor onboard.py to dispatch via provider registry.
items.notes: Phase 3 done. ABC in extraction/providers/, CA provider extracted, onboard.py dispatches via registry. 17 new tests + 61 existing all pass. Adding a new state = config entry + provider file + factory registration.

items.name: all_california_coverage
items.description: Expand Civera instance discovery beyond 3 counties (Marin, Sonoma, Yolo). Add CA SOS county breakdown as universal fallback for non-Civera counties. Script to probe CA county registrar sites for GraphQL endpoints.
items.notes: Phase 4 done. Probed all 58 CA counties — discovered San Joaquin (electionstats.sjgov.org, 2 elections 2024). Only 4/58 counties have Civera. CA SOS county_breakdown=True flag added for non-Civera counties as primary local race data source. 20 provider tests + 61 detection tests pass.

items.name: texas_election_support
items.description: Add Texas as second supported state. StateElectionConfig for TX (March primary, 30-day registration, 17-day early voting, no universal VBM). TexasElectionProvider with detect_election_sources(). TX SOS client if API accessible. End-to-end test with a TX jurisdiction.
items.notes: Phase 5. First non-CA state validates the abstraction. TX senate: 31 seats, odd=2026/even=2028. Statewide: Gov, Lt Gov, AG, Comptroller, Land Commissioner, Ag Commissioner, Railroad Commissioner. ~1.5 sessions.

items.name: florida_election_support
items.description: Add Florida election support. StateElectionConfig + provider + SOS client. FL uses Clarity Elections (Scytl) widely — building that client covers many FL counties.
items.notes: Phase 6a. Clarity Elections platform is used by GA, NC + hundreds of counties — building it here has outsized value. Deprioritized pending CA depth completion. If non_civera_local_race_research validates Clarity, this item's priority increases (shared client covers CA counties too). ~1 session.

items.name: new_york_election_support
items.description: Add New York election support. StateElectionConfig + provider + SOS client. NY Board of Elections has public data downloads.
items.notes: Phase 6b. ~1 session.

items.name: pennsylvania_election_support
items.description: Add Pennsylvania election support. StateElectionConfig + provider + SOS client.
items.notes: Phase 6c. ~1 session.

items.name: illinois_election_support
items.description: Add Illinois election support. StateElectionConfig + provider + SOS client.
items.notes: Phase 6d. ~1 session.

turnkey_onboarding.description: 100% automated city onboarding: any US city with a supported meeting platform should go from zero to fully queryable in one command. Blocking all downstream work (federation queries, billing, operator adoption).

items.name: civicclerk_pipeline_wiring
items.description: Wire CivicClerk client into fetch_meetings() in modal_ingest.py. Client exists (civicclerk.py), just needs elif branch + SUPPORTED_MEETING_SOURCES registration. Same pattern as legistar_client.
items.notes: CivicClerk uses OData API. Cities: El Cerrito, Hayward, San Pablo. ~1 session. Follow legistar_client pattern exactly.

items.name: escribe_pipeline_wiring
items.description: Wire eScribe client into fetch_meetings() in modal_ingest.py. Client exists (escribe.py), needs elif branch + SUPPORTED_MEETING_SOURCES registration. Covers Canadian cities + National City CA.
items.notes: Pipeline wiring done. eScribe sites have SSL cert chain issue with Python certifi on macOS (curl works, requests fails). Needs system cert fix or Modal testing.

items.name: html_agenda_extraction
items.description: Extract chunks from HTML agendas when PDF is unavailable. Some Legistar/Granicus cities serve agendas as HTML only — chunks=0 for these cities, breaking chunk search. Detect format and route to HTML parser.
items.notes: Currently silent failure: onboarding quality report warns chunks=0 but no remediation. Need to detect HTML vs PDF agenda format and extract text content from HTML agendas into chunks. ~1-2 sessions.

items.name: onboard_quality_gates
items.description: Strengthen onboard.py quality validation: fail-fast on zero meetings, auto-retry on transient API errors, compare ratios against baseline, and generate actionable remediation steps instead of just warnings.
items.notes: Current quality report is advisory only. Should: (1) distinguish transient errors from platform limitations, (2) suggest specific fixes per failure mode, (3) gate progression to vector indexing on minimum data thresholds. ~1 session.

items.name: issue_provider_dispatch
items.description: Generalize fetch_issues() to support multiple 311 providers (SeeClickFix, FixItMarin, QAlert, etc.) via source-type dispatch — same pattern as fetch_meetings(). Add SUPPORTED_ISSUE_SOURCES registry. Currently hardcoded to SeeClickFix.
items.notes: fetch_issues() is hardcoded to SeeClickFixClient. Needs the same config-driven dispatch pattern as meetings: load jurisdiction YAML → read issues source_type → route to correct client. Cities change 311 providers (e.g., Marin County switching to FixItMarin). YAML should specify provider, not assume SeeClickFix. ~1 session.

items.name: issue_provider_detection
items.description: Auto-detect 311/issue provider during onboarding discovery. Probe known APIs (SeeClickFix, FixItMarin, QAlert) by city/county name, write detected provider to extraction config JSON. Provider can change over time — detection is re-runnable via --detect-issues.
items.notes: detect_issue_source() probes SeeClickFix API by city name. Wired into onboard_jurisdiction() flow and --detect-issues CLI flag for re-running. Future providers (FixItMarin, QAlert) add probes after the SeeClickFix block.

items.name: onboard_transcript_auto
items.description: Auto-detect YouTube channels for meeting recordings during onboarding. Probe YouTube Data API for city council channels, add to jurisdiction YAML if found. Gated on AssemblyAI key availability.
items.notes: Many cities post recordings to YouTube. Detection could use YouTube search API by city name + 'city council'. Only enable transcription if AssemblyAI key is configured. ~1 session.

items.name: onboard_end_to_end_test
items.description: Integration test for the full onboarding pipeline: mock city with Legistar source, run onboard.py, verify all stages complete (discovery → config → fetch → store → index → quality report). Catches regressions.
items.notes: Currently no automated test for the onboarding pipeline. Manual testing catches issues but doesn't prevent regressions. Use mock Legistar API responses. ~1 session.

items.name: onboard_deploy_integration
items.description: Wire onboard.py to trigger Modal deployment after successful ingestion. Currently onboarding populates Postgres but doesn't deploy or update the live API. Should optionally deploy and verify the city is queryable.
items.notes: Phase 3.5 added: registry update (always) + Modal deploy + API verification (with --deploy flag). 12 new tests.

items.name: onboard_batch_mode
items.description: Support onboarding multiple cities in a single command. Iterate over a list of jurisdiction IDs, run discovery + ingestion for each, produce aggregate quality report. Enables rapid expansion.
items.notes: For scaling beyond one-at-a-time onboarding. Takes a file or list of jurisdiction IDs, runs them sequentially with shared config. Useful for 'onboard all Marin cities' or 'onboard all Legistar CA cities'. ~1 session.

items.name: onboard_configurable_defaults
items.description: Read days_past and sample_days defaults from jurisdiction YAML (ingestion.days_past, ingestion.sample_days) so operators can tune per-city. CLI flags override YAML. Falls back to current hardcoded defaults (365/30).
items.notes: Small change: read YAML in Phase 2 after configs exist, apply as defaults before Phase 2.5. ~0.5 session.

items.name: onboard_cost_estimate
items.description: After the validation sample, extrapolate meeting counts to the full backfill window and estimate LLM cost (agenda + decision extraction) before proceeding. Print estimate and prompt for confirmation unless --yes flag is passed.
items.notes: Use sample meeting count to extrapolate: meetings_in_sample * (days_past / sample_days). Cost model from modal_ingest.py docstring: ~$0.02/meeting for fetch, ~$0.05/meeting for LLM extraction. Add --yes flag to auto-proceed. ~1 session.

items.name: require_created_at_on_writes
items.description: All relay write endpoints must require created_at and reject writes without it. Currently Optional[int] = None, omitting it skips signature verification entirely.

items.name: amlegal_client_hardening

items.notes: Parser tested on 4 cities. Sacramento stored (5,871 sections) + vectorized (9,224 embeddings). Turnkey onboard tested end-to-end: fixed 6 issues in modal_ingest.py, onboard.py, american_legal.py, and municipal.py for graceful handling of unsupported platforms, AMLegal cache mounting on Modal, and jurisdiction registry gaps.

acceptance_policy.description: Relay acceptance policy enforcement — attestation verification and rate limiting hardening (Phases 2-3 from spec)

items.name: http_ip_rate_limiting
items.description: Add HTTP-level per-IP rate limiting on relay before crypto verification. First line of defense against spam.

items.name: nip13_proof_of_work
items.description: Add NIP-13 proof-of-work requirement for rate-limited (free) tier writes. 20-bit target ~1s computation. Provides sybil resistance for the free tier.
items.notes: _verify_pow wired into check() as tier 3, before rate limiting. Valid PoW bypasses rate limit. Configured per event type via pow_difficulty.

items.name: relay_write_metadata_table
items.description: Create relay_write_metadata table to store acceptance_tier per write. Avoids modifying frozen Voice model. Clients can filter/weight by tier.
items.notes: Implemented as coordination_write_metadata table

items.name: attestation_proof_on_requests
items.description: Add attestation_proof field to CastVoiceRequest and other write request schemas. Currently missing — prerequisite for attestation enforcement.
items.notes: attestation_proof added to Voice model and request schemas

items.name: wire_attestation_verification
items.description: Wire existing verify_attestation_proof() into acceptance policy check on all write endpoints. Look up trusted issuer pubkey from issuer_registry table.
items.notes: _verify_attestation wired to extract jurisdiction from j-tag, look up issuer via issuer_lookup callable, then call verify_attestation_proof(). app.py lifespan provides issuer_lookup from storage.issuers. Falls through gracefully when no issuer_lookup configured.

items.name: config_driven_rate_limits
items.description: Move DEFAULT_POLICY from hardcoded module-level constant to per-jurisdiction configuration (config file or DB table). Currently every relay instance has identical rate limits and PoW difficulty regardless of jurisdiction.
items.notes: load_policy() resolves: RELAY_POLICY_FILE env var → config/relay_policies.json[jurisdiction] → file defaults → DEFAULT_POLICY. Deep merge preserves per-event-type fields. AcceptancePolicy accepts jurisdiction_id param, RelayConfig reads RELAY_JURISDICTION env var. 10 new tests.

items.name: extension_pow_generation
items.description: Add NIP-13 proof-of-work generation to browser extension for free-tier writes. Server-side PoW verification is wired but no client generates it — dead code path until this ships.
items.notes: minePoW() in civicos-client adds NIP-13 nonce tag. castVoice() and castComment() mine transparently when no attestation proof. 16-bit difficulty, ~650ms avg on desktop. Cross-verified against Python server-side _verify_pow(). Extension builds clean.

items.name: attestation_expiry
items.description: Add attestation expiry check: created_at + validity_period > now. Recommend 1-year validity. Design revocation mechanism (blocklist of revoked attestation event IDs).

items.name: extension_402_handling
items.description: Update extension to handle HTTP 402 responses from relay gracefully. Show UX guidance for attestation or payment options.

token_issuance.description: Blinded token payment system for relay writes — privacy-preserving per-action billing (Phase 4 from spec)

items.name: blind_signature_scheme_design
items.description: Design blind signature scheme using existing secp256k1 primitives. Define token format, blinding protocol, and spent-token storage.
items.notes: Schnorr blind sigs on secp256k1 via coincurve. SpentTokenStorage protocol with Postgres + InMemory impls.

items.name: token_issuance_service
items.description: Implement token issuance service (separate from relay). Accepts Stripe/Lightning payment, returns blinded tokens. Cannot link issued tokens to payment session.
items.notes: TokenIssuer class with 2-step Schnorr blind signing protocol, Wagner's attack mitigation (max 5 concurrent sessions), session expiry, batch issuance. AcceptancePolicy wired with spent_token_storage and known_token_issuers in app.py. 25 tests including full integration flow. Stripe payment verification deferred to extension_token_wallet phase.

items.name: payment_proof_on_models
items.description: Add payment_proof: Optional[dict] to Voice, Comment, CivicActionEvent, CivicCommitment, CivicCompletion models and their request schemas.
items.notes: payment_proof added to Voice model

items.name: token_verification_in_policy
items.description: Add token verification + spent-token tracking to acceptance policy. Atomic: token must be marked spent BEFORE write is persisted.

items.name: extension_token_wallet
items.description: Add token wallet to browser extension. Store blinded tokens in local-wallet.ts (already handles secp256k1). Include tokens in write requests automatically.
items.notes: Full client-side blind signature implementation: blind.ts ports blind()/unblind()/verifyToken() from Python using @noble/curves secp256k1 point arithmetic. token-wallet.ts provides persistent chrome.storage.local token storage with requestTokens() 2-step issuer protocol. Service worker handles GET_TOKEN_COUNT/REQUEST_TOKENS/SPEND_TOKEN messages. SidePanel auto-attaches payment_proof to castVoice(). Server-side: token issuer HTTP endpoints (/coordination/tokens/{info,session,sign}) added to app.py, coordination.py accepts payment_proof as alternative to attestation_proof with full token verification and double-spend check.

items.name: token_purchase_ui
items.description: Token purchase flow in extension: Stripe checkout -> blinded tokens, and (future) Lightning -> blinded tokens.

items.name: token_issuer_env_config
items.description: Make TokenIssuer deployment parameters configurable via env vars: TOKEN_ISSUER_SECRET (issuer private key), TOKEN_ISSUER_MAX_SESSIONS (Wagner's attack cap, default 5), TOKEN_ISSUER_SESSION_TTL (nonce expiry in seconds, default 300). Wire into issuer service deployment (Modal). Add to civicos-secrets. Document token endpoints and env vars.
items.source: configuration critic — flagged in sessions 2026-03-22 (token_issuance_service, extension_token_wallet)
items.notes: Complete. Modal secret 'civicos-token-issuer' created with TOKEN_ISSUER_SECRET, TOKEN_ISSUER_MAX_SESSIONS, TOKEN_ISSUER_SESSION_TTL, TOKEN_ISSUER_PUBKEYS. Wired into get_relay_secrets(). items.name: marin_sibling_ingestion
items.description: Build a turnkey onboard-and-ingest flow, validate it by onboarding Mill Valley and San Anselmo end-to-end, then update docs so any operator can do the same.
items.source: federation testbed — data prerequisite for cross_marin_query_prototype + operator experience validation
items.notes: Done 2026-03-15. Turnkey onboard script (scripts/onboard.py) generates configs + runs Modal ingestion in one command. Mill Valley: 57 meetings, 166 agenda items, 2 decisions, 591 vectors. San Anselmo: 152 meetings, 34 new agenda items, 112 decisions, 1037 vectors. Both jurisdictions now have non-zero decisions + vectors. Chunks were 0/14 due to Granicus HTML agendas (MV) and SSL cert errors (SA) — not blocking.

items.name: turnkey_onboard_hardening
items.description: Add a validation gate (small sample + quality check before full backfill) and fix data quality gaps: HTML agenda chunk extraction for Granicus, duplicate meeting deduplication, post-onboard quality report, and idempotent re-runs.
items.source: marin_sibling_ingestion validation — gaps found during Mill Valley + San Anselmo onboarding
items.notes: Eight gaps identified: (0) No validation gate — ingests 365 days blind, should sample 30 days first, verify quality (chunks>0? decisions>0?), then scale up only if quality passes. Prevents burning $3-4 on jurisdictions with unextractable data. (1) Chunks=0 for Granicus HTML AgendaViewer sites — need to extract text from GeneratedAgendaViewer HTML pages when no PDF link exists. (2) Only 2/57 decisions for Mill Valley — thin HTML minutes, need quality signal. (3) Duplicate meetings from multi-view archives — view 2 and 3 contain same meetings, wastes LLM spend. (4) No post-onboard quality report — operator can't tell if results are good or bad. (5) County enrichment is fragile string patching on YAML. (6) No idempotency — re-run doubles LLM spend on agenda/decisions. (7) City name sensitivity — slug derivation is case/prefix sensitive. Must fix before open sourcing and before cross-jurisdiction queries can rely on this data.

Data ready: SR 83 decisions, MV 60, SA 96. Decision IDs migrated to meeting-scoped ordinals (f08025f). Remaining: (1) downward resolution — query county-marin should fan out to child cities, (2) cache registry.json in memory, (3) mount v2 on REST API server.

items.description: Add eScribe platform client to close the last platform coverage gap (Portland, OR). Implement BaseExtractor, add to factory + platform_detection discovery. Enables turnkey onboarding for eScribe-based jurisdictions.
items.source: platform coverage gap — Portland OR uses eScribe, only unsupported platform found in stress testing
items.notes: Portland OR is the only major US city that failed platform discovery. eScribe is used by Portland and other Pacific NW cities. Existing abstraction (BaseExtractor + factory + discovery) is already generalizable — just needs a new client implementation.

items.name: cross_county_query_prototype
items.description: Prototype cross-county queries: Berkeley (Alameda) vs San Rafael (Marin). Test relevance filtering — when are cross-county results useful vs noise?
items.notes: also_include field added to SearchRequest (d2d20f4), jurisdiction ID validation (622423b). Validated 5 spec questions with real data. 138 tests pass. Remaining: officially onboard Marin cities and cross-county jurisdictions before marking done.

items.name: pagination_protocol_update
items.description: Add limit/offset parameters to StorageBackend.get_*() methods. Informed by real cross-jurisdiction query patterns from testbed.
items.notes: Mechanical change but touches every backend implementation. Easier to do now with 2 backends than later with N. Prerequisite for FederatedDataSource fan-out.

items.name: query_monitoring_and_docs
items.description: Production polish: query latency logging, connection pool metrics, alert thresholds, and docs sweep to update stale decision ID format references across ~10 doc files.
items.notes: Docs: entity_id_namespace.md updated but ~10 other files still reference old decision:{jur}:{date}:{item} format. Monitoring: per-corpus query times already logged but not persisted or alerted on.

items.name: multi_issuer_lookup
items.description: Update issuer_lookup signature from (jurisdiction) -> Optional[str] to (jurisdiction) -> List[TrustedIssuer] with validity windows and trust levels. Informed by testbed findings.
items.notes: Current single-pubkey return is too simple for cross-county trust. With 3 test issuers, can validate the new signature before going live.

items.name: federation_adr
items.description: Write Architecture Decision Record documenting federation boundaries: which protocols change, which stay, execution model for cross-jurisdiction queries, and trust chain design.
items.notes: Written after testbed findings, not before. This ADR should reflect what was learned, not what was assumed.

items.name: simbli_discovery_integration
items.description: Wire existing SimbliClient into discovery chain (factory, platform_detection, onboard). Make BaseExtractor-compatible. Simbli serves school boards via Playwright-based scraping at simbli.eboardsolutions.com.

items.name: universal_adapter_design
items.description: Design session: LLM-powered universal adapter for cities with custom platforms (Portland, NYC). Research declarative scraping configs, LLM-inferred selectors, failure modes. Output: ADR + prototype design.

items.name: v2_adapter_storage_refactor
items.description: Refactored v2 corpus adapters to call storage/vector backends directly. Removed CivicOS middleman. Cross-jurisdiction no longer creates CivicOS instances.
items.source: architectural review — v2 query layer cleanup
items.notes: Cross-jurisdiction testing (2026-03-14) hit connection pool exhaustion and cold-start thundering herd from creating CivicOS instances per jurisdiction. Current workarounds (shared backends, warm-then-fan-out, 20s timeout) are duct tape. Removing the CivicOS middleman is the clean fix.

items.name: direct_city_submission
items.description: Authenticated endpoint for city clerks to submit meeting data directly (PDF upload + metadata). Bypasses scraping entirely. Extension UI for drag-and-drop upload.
items.source: onboarding friction — scraping is fragile, cities already have the data
items.notes: Trivial implementation: POST endpoint accepts {title, date, board, pdf_file}, runs AgendaPacketParser, calls store_meetings() + store_chunks(). Auth via API key per jurisdiction. Extension gets Upload Agenda button. Scraping pipeline remains as fallback for historical data and non-adopting cities. 1-2 sessions of work.

items.name: onboarding_yaml_generation
items.description: Extend onboard.py to generate complete jurisdiction YAML (refresh policies, contact info, hierarchy, modal config) in addition to extraction JSON. Makes onboarding produce all config needed for a functioning jurisdiction.
items.notes: onboard.py currently generates extraction JSON but not jurisdiction YAML. YAML needed for refresh policies, modal deployment config, contact info. ~1 session.

items.name: legistar_client
items.description: Wire Legistar meeting fetch into Modal ingestion pipeline. Sacramento has 35 discovered bodies (extraction config exists). Enables turnkey onboard for Legistar cities (Sacramento, Oakland, SF, etc.).
items.notes: Wired legistar source_type into fetch_meetings() (modal_ingest.py), added to SUPPORTED_MEETING_SOURCES registry. Fixed datetime parsing for 12-hour time format. 42 Sacramento meetings verified via live API. 6 unit tests.

multi_scale_participation.description: Civic participation at every government level — federal comment periods, state legislative hearings, and cross-scale query support

items.name: extension_tab_fix
items.description: Fix CA/Federal extension tabs that show loading/error state because no servers exist at those endpoints. Either route existing what_applies() legislation data to those tabs, or hide tabs gracefully until servers are deployed.
items.notes: Extension calls getCityPulseFromServer() on california.civicosproject.org and federal.civicosproject.org, which don't exist. what_applies() data (LegiScan, Federal Register) already comes through the city's LegislationAdapter on the city tab. Quick fix: show that data on parent tabs instead of calling nonexistent servers. 1 session.

items.name: federal_comment_periods
items.description: Ingest federal comment periods from regulations.gov API. Store as upcoming events with deadlines. Enable civic.act submission. Highest-value federal participation surface.
items.notes: regulations.gov has a well-documented REST API (api.regulations.gov). Comment periods have structured deadlines, map cleanly to civic.upcoming (type=comment_periods) and civic.act (action=submit_comment). Need: (1) API client for open comment periods, (2) store as upcoming events with deadline dates, (3) civic.act handler that formats and submits comments. UpcomingType.comment_periods enum already exists but nothing implements it. 1-2 sessions.

items.name: federal_funding_pipeline
items.description: Bulk ingest federal awards via USAspending API for all configured jurisdictions. Client exists (usaspending.py), API is free. Store in federal_awards table, add to weekly refresh, index vectors.
items.source: multi-scale participation — federal data (plan: docs/internal/federal-data-plan.md, sessions 1-2)
items.notes: Currently 5 awards totaling $17.2M for San Rafael. USAspending API supports geographic filtering, no key needed. Target: hundreds of awards across all Marin jurisdictions. Session 2: build FundingAdapter for v2 search, wire into civic.upcoming for expiring grants, add to extension.

items.name: congressional_votes
items.description: Extend CongressGovClient with vote retrieval. Store in congressional_votes table linked to legislation + elected_officials.
items.notes: DONE: CongressGovClient extended with House Clerk XML + Senate XML parsing. congressional_votes table + storage protocol. 1,491 votes ingested (173 House/Huffman, 1318 Senate/Schiff+Padilla). Added to weekly refresh.

items.name: congressional_votes_query
items.description: Wire congressional votes into v2 query layer, MCP tool, and extension. Enable 'How did my representative vote on [bill]?' queries.
items.notes: 1,491 votes in DB. Wire into v2 search (civic.search 'housing votes'), MCP get_congressional_votes tool, extension 'How They Voted' view on Federal tab. Parallels city council get_voting_record.

items.name: congressional_hearings
items.description: Ingest congressional committee hearings from Congress.gov API. Store as events, wire into civic.upcoming alongside comment periods. Federal equivalent of city council meetings.
items.notes: COMPLETE. Session 1: 421 hearings ingested (274 House, 147 Senate). Session 2: Wired into v2 search (CongressionalHearingsAdapter), upcoming verb (congressional_hearings event type), MCP tool (get_congressional_hearings), extension UX (Congressional Hearings section in pulse), and city_pulse data. All verified against live data.

items.name: local_impact_relevance
items.description: Score federal rules by local relevance. Agency-to-topic mapping, geographic text matching, CFR part matching. Extension sorts by relevance, draft_federal_comment shows local context.
items.notes: COMPLETE. Created relevance.py with 3 heuristic signals: (1) agency-to-topic mapping (24 agencies → 13 local policy areas), (2) geographic text matching (San Rafael/Marin/Bay Area/California with tiered weighting), (3) CFR title matching (14 locally relevant CFR titles). Added local_relevance_score FLOAT + relevance_reasons JSONB columns to federal_rules table. Backfilled 4,115 rules: 1,013 scored > 0 (25%). Scores auto-computed on ingest via store_federal_rules(). V2 search sorts federal comment periods by relevance. MCP tools display relevance score + reasons. Chunker includes relevance context in vector text for semantic search.

items.name: vector_llm_relevance_pipeline
items.description: Vector-first relevance pipeline: embed local policy descriptions as query vectors, retrieve candidate federal rules by similarity, LLM-confirm relevance on candidates only. Replaces heuristic-only scoring with semantic + LLM hybrid.
items.source: multi-scale participation — federal data (refinement of local_impact_relevance)
items.notes: 3-stage pipeline: (1) Define 10-15 policy area query vectors for San Rafael (can bootstrap from existing municipal_code embeddings — tested and works, 0.69 similarity for housing, 0.68 for water). (2) For each policy vector, retrieve top 30-50 most similar federal rules via pgvector cosine similarity, deduplicate across policy areas (~200-400 candidates from 4,115 total). (3) Send candidates to gpt-4o-mini in batches of 20-30 for confirmation + local_relevance_summary generation. Store score + summary. Cost: ~$0.05 for full corpus, pennies/week for new rules. Follows existing classify_topics.py batch pattern. Ongoing: new rules auto-scored on ingest after embedding. 1-2 sessions.

items.name: federal_pipeline_hardening
items.description: Fix US legislation refresh gap (only CA syncs), debug CA sync failure, close 12% embedding gap on federal_rules, verify all new corpora have scheduled refreshes.
items.notes: Done: (1) Added US federal legislation to scheduled_low_velocity_refresh loop alongside CA. (2) CA sync confirmed working (last cron success 2026-03-15). (3) Created expand_federal_rules_to_chunks() in chunker.py — adds document_type, topics, fallback text for rules without title/abstract, closing embedding gap. (4) Added 'legislation' to federal-US corpus types in index_vectors. All 8 federal corpora now have scheduled refreshes.

items.name: federal_server_deployment
items.description: Deploy country-united-states Modal server with full federal tool suite: funding search, congressional votes, hearing timeline, relevance-scored comment periods.
items.notes: Meaningful after sessions 1-9 create real federal-specific tools and data. Federal server becomes the peer that city MCPs federate with when the shared DB splits. Create civicos-federal-env Modal secret. 1 session.

items.name: state_legislative_client
items.description: Build California legislature data client using leginfo.legislature.ca.gov. Ingest committee hearing schedules, bill status with vote dates, public comment windows.
items.notes: Uses official bulk downloads from downloads.leginfo.legislature.ca.gov (same format as modal_cacode.py). Parses BILL_TBL, BILL_VERSION_TBL, BILL_HISTORY_TBL, BILL_SUMMARY_VOTE_TBL, COMMITTEE_HEARING_TBL, COMMITTEE_AGENDA_TBL. Initial ingest: 4,248 AB/SB bills + 73,721 events (hearings, votes, history). Special session bills use -x1 suffix. Daily deltas available for refresh.

items.name: state_server_deployment
items.description: Deploy state-california Modal server. Wire committee hearings, bill votes, and comment windows into the server's data. Connect extension CA tab.
items.notes: Deployed 2026-03-21. Direct URL: lounsburynw--civicos-california-mcpserver-mcp-endpoint.modal.run. 24 tools (state+federal). Fixed: Modal secret ordering (primary last), REST API register endpoint type annotation, CA legislation cron secret name. Cloudflare proxy (california.civicosproject.org) still routes to stale old deploy — needs DNS/Worker update to point to new Modal URL. Weekly cron registered (Sunday 4 AM UTC). Extension CA tab has voice/coordination support but not state-specific content rendering (acceptable for MVP).

items.name: vertical_query_tier_tuning
items.description: Tune tier weights for upward queries (city→state→federal). Parent tier is currently 1.0 (same as self), which means state/federal results compete equally with local decisions. May need level-aware weighting or separate result grouping.
items.notes: With real state/federal data, include_parents=True will return results from 3+ levels. Questions: (1) Should parent weight stay 1.0 or decrease with distance (county=0.9, state=0.7, federal=0.5)? (2) Should jurisdiction_results group by level (local/state/federal) not just jurisdiction ID? (3) How does the extension render mixed-level results? Needs real data to validate — run after federal_comment_periods. 1 session.

items.name: downward_query_scaling
items.description: Cap or paginate downward resolution for state/county-level queries. Querying state-california with include_siblings (downward) would fan out to every CA city — works with 4, breaks with hundreds.
items.notes: Options: (1) cap fan-out at N jurisdictions (e.g., 10), (2) require explicit also_include for large fan-outs, (3) aggregate mode returns counts per jurisdiction without full search. Not urgent until CA has more than ~10 cities. 1 session.

items.name: upcoming_comment_periods
items.description: Implement UpcomingType.comment_periods and UpcomingType.hearings in civic.upcoming. Surface federal comment deadlines and state hearing dates alongside local meetings.
items.notes: UpcomingType enum already has comment_periods and hearings but execute_upcoming() only handles meetings. Need adapters that query stored comment periods/hearings with deadlines. Key UX: show 'Comment period closes in 3 days' alongside 'City Council meets Tuesday'. 1 session, depends on federal_comment_periods data.

items.name: civic_act_federal_comment
items.description: civic.act handlers for federal comment drafting and submission preparation. draft_federal_comment returns structured draft guidance with rule context; prepare_federal_comment returns submission URL, deadline, and instructions. Programmatic submission not supported by regulations.gov — users submit via web form.
items.notes: regulations.gov does not support programmatic POST comment submission (ToS restriction). Implemented draft_federal_comment (AI-assisted draft with stance-aware guidance, rule context, deadline urgency) and prepare_federal_comment (structured submission context for extension UI). Both wired into civic.act via _ACTION_TO_HANDLER, registered as MCP tools in FEDERAL_TOOLS, and ref-parseable from rule:us-federal:{doc_number}.

items.name: legislation_adapter_unification
items.description: Unify legislation data path: query stored state/federal legislation first, fall back to what_applies() API calls. Currently all legislation comes via on-demand API calls regardless of what's stored.
items.notes: LegislationAdapter currently calls what_applies() which hits LegiScan/Federal Register APIs on every query. With stored state/federal data, should check storage first for faster responses and offline capability. API calls become the refresh mechanism, not the query path. 1 session.

items.name: turnkey_state_onboarding
items.description: Generalize state-level onboarding beyond hardcoded CA. Framework for adding other states (legislation source detection, bulk download client generation, server deployment).
items.notes: CA is hardcoded to leginfo.legislature.ca.gov. Other states have different legislation platforms. Deprioritized per roadmap — CA is the only state needed pre-launch. Post-launch work.

election_integration.description: Election data and school board platform integration — surface candidates, ballot measures, deadlines, results, and school board agendas for Bay Area residents. Built on research from docs/internal/election-data-research.md.

items.name: election_data_source_research
items.description: Research session: audit election data sources (Google Civic API, BallotReady, Ballotpedia, county registrars) and school board platforms (Simbli, BoardDocs) for Bay Area. Determine which sources to wire into turnkey onboarding.
items.notes: Research only — no code changes. Focus on Bay Area first. Verify existing clients, survey alternatives, define integration model for elections and school boards.

items.name: democracy_works_client
items.description: Build DemocracyWorksClient in extraction clients. REST v2 API — elections, candidates, ballot measures, deadlines, polling locations. BLOCKED: pricing unknown (sales-gated, no free tier). Must confirm nonprofit access before building.
items.notes: BLOCKED on pricing — sales-gated, no public free tier. Email partnerships@democracy.works to ask about nonprofit access. Do not build until pricing confirmed. If too expensive, skip and rely on Marin Registrar + CA SOS + existing Google Civic for election data.

items.name: marin_registrar_results_client
items.description: Build GraphQL client for pastelections.marincounty.gov (ElectionStats/Civera platform). Historical local election results 2010-2025: 46 elections, 521 contests, 1,404 candidates with vote counts, precinct breakdowns, ballot measures. Three-query pattern: list elections, list contests, get precinct data.
items.notes: NOT a CSV scraper — the site has a public GraphQL API at POST /api/graphql_pr. No auth needed. Extend existing marin_registrar.py. May need to add votes_received to Candidate model. See docs/internal/election-data-research.md for full GraphQL reference. ~1 session.

items.name: boarddocs_client
items.description: Build BoardDocsClient for school board meeting ingestion. Covers MCOE, Ross Valley SD, Larkspur-Corte Madera SD, Sausalito-Marin City SD, Marin Community College. Uses undocumented POST endpoints (BD-GetMeetingsList, PRINT-AgendaDetailed). Reference impl: llama-index-readers-boarddocs.
items.notes: No auth needed. POST to /BD-GetMeetingsList?open returns JSON meeting list. POST to /PRINT-AgendaDetailed returns HTML agenda. Register as source_type boarddocs in factory. Config: app_path (e.g. ca/rova) + committee_id. ~1-2 sessions.

items.name: simbli_district_expansion
items.description: Onboard 6 additional Marin school districts via existing Simbli client: Novato USD (S=36030351), Tamalpais Union HSD (S=36030468), Miller Creek SD, Mill Valley SD, Reed Union SD, Kentfield SD. Config-only — client already works.
items.notes: Complete. 6 extraction configs created, 6 registry entries added, simbli added to SUPPORTED_MEETING_SOURCES, fetch_simbli_meetings() Modal function with Playwright image, simbli dispatch in fetch_meetings(). Novato+Tamalpais use simbli.eboardsolutions.com (S= codes), other 4 use agendaonline.net. All configs load + factory dispatch verified.

items.name: ca_sos_results_client
items.description: Wire CA Secretary of State Results API (api.sos.ca.gov) for state-level race results with Marin County breakdowns. No auth required, JSON responses. Covers governor, legislature, US Congress, state propositions.
items.notes: Complete. 53 unit + 5 integration tests passing. Client covers statewide races, district races, ballot measures, county breakdowns, and reporting status. Storage mappers + Modal ingestion wired. Live API confirmed working.

items.name: election_source_config
items.description: Add election_sources field to extraction configs. Update scheduled_election_refresh() to read per-jurisdiction election provider config and dispatch to Google Civic, Marin Registrar, and CA SOS as configured.
items.notes: Schema-first: define election_sources field, update scheduled_election_refresh() to read it, populate for existing jurisdictions. Must land before ca_sos_pipeline_wiring. ~1 session.

items.name: ca_sos_pipeline_wiring
items.description: Wire CA SOS results into monthly election cron. fetch_ca_sos_election_results() Modal function exists but is not called by scheduled_election_refresh(). Add dispatch for jurisdictions with ca_sos_results in election_sources.
items.notes: Depends on election_source_config. The Modal function and storage mappers already exist — this is wiring, not client work. Default: run for state-california with county breakdowns for Marin. ~0.5 session.

items.name: school_district_lookup
items.description: Static lookup table (data/school_districts.json) mapping county -> school districts with platform URLs. Enable onboard.py --level school --city 'Novato' and --county 'Marin' --level school for batch onboarding.
items.notes: Seed from existing data/extraction/school-*.json configs (10 Marin districts). Future: scrape CDE CALPADS API to auto-populate other counties.

items.name: onboard_election_detection
items.description: Auto-detect election data sources during city/county onboarding. After geocoding, probe Google Civic, CA SOS, and county registrar availability. Populate election_sources in extraction config automatically.
items.notes: detect_election_sources() + _infer_division_name() wired into onboard flow after geocoding (Step 3.6). 23 unit tests. School district names resolved via school_districts.json lookup.

items.name: google_civic_deprecation
items.description: Removed Google Civic client entirely. Representatives endpoint dead since April 2025, Elections endpoint returns minimal data. State-specific sources (CA SOS, Marin Registrar) provide better coverage.
items.notes: Full removal instead of deprecation. Representatives already handled by RepresentativesClient (Congress.gov + LegiScan). Elections handled by state-specific sources. detect_election_sources() no longer includes google_civic. Extraction configs updated.

items.name: cde_school_directory
items.description: Build statewide school district lookup from CA Dept of Education directory. Fetch CDE district list, probe each district website for Simbli/BoardDocs platforms, and generate school_districts.json entries. Enables turnkey --level school onboarding for any CA county, not just Marin.
items.notes: CDE publishes district directory (name, county, website). Probe each website against _detect_simbli() and _detect_boarddocs() in platform_detection.py. Parallelizable — ~2 requests per district. One-time build script, output extends existing school_districts.json structure. ~1 session.

items.name: multi_county_registrar_research
items.description: Research CA county registrar systems beyond Marin. Identified 3 counties using Civera ElectionStats (Marin, Sonoma, Yolo). Built generalized CiveraElectionStatsClient, extraction configs, and Modal fetch function. 141 elections across 3 counties.

items.name: upcoming_ballot_preview
items.description: Built CA SOS ballot preview client: downloads certified candidate PDFs from SOS CDN, parses candidate name/party/ballot-designation/contact using pymupdf, maps to storage format. Supports all 8 race types (congress, state-senate, assembly, governor, lt-governor, controller, treasurer, attorney-general). 107 candidates across 8 contests stored for San Rafael. Wired into Modal ingest (--ballot-preview flag) and extraction config.
items.notes: Phase 1 complete: CA SOS PDF parser. Phase 2 (future): Marin Registrar candidate filings + local ballot measures. Phase 3 (future): deadline scraping from registrar. See docs/internal/election-data-research.md.

election_coverage_lifecycle.description: Deepen CA election data to every locale, automate election data flow on city onboard, and implement calendar-aware ingestion. Priority order: CA depth first, automation second, ingestion strategy third. See docs/internal/election-coverage-assessment.md.

items.name: ca_sos_snapshot_archival
items.description: Archive CA SOS election results before overwrite. On each scheduled_election_refresh() run, diff election_id against previous snapshot. If changed, preserve old data with timestamp before fetching new. Converts the ephemeral SOS API into a persistent historical archive.
items.notes: SOS get_reporting_status() returns current election metadata. Snapshot = store results keyed by {election_id}:{timestamp} instead of overwriting. Cheapest way to gain historical coverage for state races. ~1 session.

items.name: backfill_election_sources
items.description: Run detect_election_sources() for the 24 extraction configs that lack election_sources. One-time script or --re-detect flag on onboard. All CA jurisdictions get at minimum ca_sos_results + legislative districts. School districts get state-level coverage.
items.notes: 24 configs currently have zero election data. Most are CA jurisdictions. Quick win: all get statewide + district race coverage. ~0.5 session.

items.name: populate_deadlines_in_cron
items.description: Wire generate_deadlines() into scheduled_election_refresh(). After election data is stored for each jurisdiction, generate deadlines from StateElectionConfig offsets and store via store_election_deadlines(). Currently only 3 pilot jurisdictions have deadlines (from manual seed script).
items.notes: seed_election_calendar.py demonstrates the pattern. The cron needs the same 3 lines: generate, convert, store. ~0.5 session.

items.name: civera_periodic_discovery
items.description: Schedule quarterly re-probe of CA counties for new Civera ElectionStats instances. Script exists (probe_civera_counties.py). Needs scheduling via GitHub Actions and auto-update of civera_instances.json. Currently 4/58 counties have Civera — new deployments could appear at any time.
items.notes: Quarterly GH Actions cron probes all 58 CA counties. Opens PR with updated civera_instances.json if new instances found. Lost instances warn but don't remove.

items.name: non_civera_local_race_research
items.description: Research paths to local race data for the 54 CA counties without Civera. Focus on Clarity Elections (Scytl) — used by many CA, FL, and GA counties for results reporting. If a Clarity client is viable, it could cover both CA depth and FL expansion with one client. Output: research doc with findings per county and platform recommendation.
items.notes: Research complete. 9 CA counties have Clarity (7 net-new beyond Civera). Data is ephemeral (XML purged after months). clarify library (MIT) exists. Client build: ~2-3 sessions for +7 counties. See docs/internal/clarity-elections-research.md.

items.name: wire_election_fetch_into_onboard
items.description: After detect_election_sources() populates the extraction config at onboard step 3.6, trigger an immediate election data fetch using provider dispatch logic. New cities get election data on day 1 instead of waiting up to 30 days for the monthly cron.
items.notes: Created election_fetch.py with fetch_elections_for_jurisdiction() — pure Python, no Modal dependency. Dispatches to Civera, CA SOS, Marin legacy, and elected officials clients. Wired into onboard step 3.6.1 with graceful failure handling.

items.name: officials_derivation_in_cron
items.description: Call derive_elected_officials() after contest data is stored in scheduled_election_refresh(). Function exists at modal_ingest.py:3973 but is never called by the cron. Complements officials_refresh_cron in representative_lookup (which covers Congress.gov/LegiScan API refresh).
items.notes: Should only derive for jurisdictions where contests were actually stored (check result counts). ~0.5 session.

items.name: election_cron_enrollment_validation
items.description: Verify get_active_jurisdictions() includes all jurisdiction types (school-*, college-*, county-*) in the election cron dispatch. Add test confirming new jurisdictions with election_sources are auto-included without manual enrollment.
items.notes: May already work. Needs validation and a test. ~0.5 session.

items.name: calendar_aware_election_refresh
items.description: Vary scheduled_election_refresh() cadence by proximity to known election dates. Daily within 7 days of election (capture election-night SOS updates). Weekly within 90 days. Monthly otherwise. Uses get_next_election_date() from cycles.py.
items.notes: GitHub Actions cron can run daily; Modal function checks election proximity internally and decides whether to fetch. Depends on ca_sos_snapshot_archival (daily refresh without archival risks duplicate overwrites). ~1 session.

items.name: ballot_preview_smart_scheduling
items.description: Trigger ballot preview fetch only in the pre-election window (~90 and ~30 days before election day). Skip outside that window. Currently runs monthly regardless. Uses election_date from ca_sos_ballot_preview config.
items.notes: Config already includes election_date. Compare today to election_date - 90d. ~0.5 session.

items.name: election_coverage_monitoring
items.description: Monthly completeness report: count elections, contests, deadlines, officials per jurisdiction. Flag jurisdictions with zero data in any category. Output to logs or GitHub issue (like existing cron-failure alerts).
items.notes: Uses get_election_count() and similar from storage protocol. Same pattern as existing cron alert workflows. ~0.5 session.

representative_lookup.description: Enable 'who represents me?' — the most common citizen query. Derive current officeholders from election winners already in storage, expose via v2 explore endpoint and MCP tool, fill local data gaps. Depends on election_integration (done).

items.name: district_detection_onboarding
items.description: Add district detection to onboard.py (new Step 3.6.1). Use Census Bureau Geocoding API (free, no auth) to resolve lat/lng → congressional district, state senate district, state assembly district. Populate 'districts' field in extraction config automatically. Also fixed county name normalization (Google Maps returns 'Marin County', now stripped to 'marin'). Backfilled Mill Valley and San Anselmo via re-onboard.
items.notes: Census Bureau geocoder (geocoding.geo.census.gov) returns GEOID for congressional, state upper/lower districts. Free, no API key. Parse GEOID to district number. Wire into detect_election_sources() or as a new detect_districts() called right after. Backfill existing configs missing districts. ~1 session.

items.name: derive_officials_from_winners
items.description: Build function to derive current elected officials from election_contests data. For each jurisdiction, find the most recent election per seat type, extract candidates with is_winner=true, and store via store_elected_officials(). Covers federal (congress), state (assembly/senate), county (supervisors) from data we already have.
items.notes: derive_officials_from_contests() in _internal/elections/derive.py. Scans elections → contests → raw_data.mapped_candidates for is_winner=True, keeps most recent per seat, maps contest_type to seat name (US House District N, State Senate District N, etc.), stores with temporal versioning. Modal function derive_elected_officials() wired. 35 tests passing. NOTE: Civera contest data not yet ingested to Postgres — run fetch_marin_election_results first to populate.

items.name: congress_gov_federal_officials
items.description: Wire CongressGovClient (already in representatives.py) to populate elected_officials table for federal legislators. Given a jurisdiction's districts config (us-rep, state-senate), fetch current members from Congress.gov API and store. Provides authoritative federal rep data independent of election results.
items.notes: DONE. RepresentativesClient now config-driven — loads state_code and districts from extraction config (data/extraction/*.json) instead of hardcoded San Rafael values. Fixed term date mapper to handle int years from Congress.gov API. Federal officials (Schiff, Padilla, Huffman) stored for all 3 pilot jurisdictions. Cleaned up 456 old LegiScan entries incorrectly stored under city-san-rafael. Also improved state legislator filtering to use jurisdiction's specific assembly/senate districts. Modal function fetch_elected_officials() works for any jurisdiction.

items.name: local_officials_curation
items.description: Manual curation of local officials (city council, mayor) for pilot jurisdictions. San Rafael city council has 5 members + mayor — curate into a static file (data/officials/) or directly into elected_officials storage. For scale: detect from Granicus/Legistar meeting body pages or BoardDocs roster HTML.
items.notes: Start with manual curation for San Rafael (5 council + 1 mayor). Future: parse council member names from Granicus meeting pages (body members list), BoardDocs board member HTML, or Legistar People API. School board members available from BoardDocs/Simbli or Civera election winners. ~0.5 session for manual, ~2 sessions for automated extraction.

items.name: explore_representatives_endpoint
items.description: Add 'representatives' target to civic.explore verb. Query get_elected_officials() for the requested jurisdiction, walk the jurisdiction hierarchy (city → county → state → federal), and return a combined roster grouped by level. Accepts optional address parameter for geocode-based lookup.
items.notes: Add 'elif what == "representatives"' branch to execute_explore(). Walk hierarchy: jid → parent county → parent state → federal. For each level, call storage.get_elected_officials(jid, current_only=True). If address provided, geocode first to resolve jurisdiction. Update capabilities response to advertise representatives. ~1 session.

items.name: mcp_who_represents_me
items.description: Add who_represents_me(address) tool to MCP server. Geocodes address → resolves jurisdictions → queries elected_officials for each level → returns combined roster with name, office, party, contact info, level. The flagship citizen query.
items.notes: Implemented as civic_who_represents_me v2 tool in server.py. Geocodes address → resolve_jurisdictions(include_parents=True) → get_elected_officials per level. Falls back to jurisdiction param or server default. Added Mill Valley + San Anselmo to geocoding mappings. 17 tests.

items.name: officials_refresh_cron
items.description: Add elected officials refresh to GitHub Actions cron. After election results are ingested, re-derive current officials from winners. Also refresh Congress.gov data monthly. Ensures officials roster stays current after elections.
items.notes: Extend existing cron-election-refresh.yml to call a new derive_officials Modal function after election ingestion completes. Monthly cadence sufficient — officials don't change often. ~0.5 session.

items.name: whats_on_my_ballot
items.description: The capstone citizen query: address → districts → which offices are up this cycle → candidates for each → measures for each jurisdiction → key dates. Combines representative_lookup (officials), ballot_awareness (calendar, measures), and district detection into one answer. Exposed as civic.explore what='my_ballot' and MCP tool whats_on_my_ballot(address).
items.notes: Implemented as explore what='my_ballot' handler. Returns elections sorted by date, contests grouped by level (federal→state→local→judicial→other), candidates from raw_data.parsed_candidates, deadlines with next_deadline computation. 16 tests passing. MCP tool description updated.

ballot_awareness.description: Election cycle intelligence — know what's on the ballot, when elections happen, and what measures mean. The data layer that feeds 'what's on my ballot?' Separate from representative_lookup (who holds office now) and election_integration (data source clients).

items.name: election_calendar
items.description: Build election cycle awareness: which seats are up when. CA has staggered terms (state senate even/odd districts alternate, assembly every 2 years, county supervisors staggered 4-year, city council staggered 4-year). Need a data model that maps office_type + district → next_election_date + term_length. Seed from CA SOS election schedule and county registrar.
items.time_sensitive: 2026-06-02 CA primary — calendar must exist to power 'what's on my ballot'
items.notes: Deterministic cycle resolver computes next election date for US House (2yr), US Senate (6yr staggered), CA Governor (4yr), Assembly (2yr), State Senate (4yr even/odd). CA deadline generator computes registration, VBM, early voting dates. Seeded June 2 primary and Nov 3 general for all 3 pilot jurisdictions with 8 contests + 5 deadlines each. 41 tests passing.

items.name: local_candidate_data
items.description: Ingest candidate data for local races (city council, county supervisor, school board). The county registrar is the authoritative source — they publish candidate filings for all local offices. Marin registrar (marincounty.gov/depts/rv) has candidate filing pages. BoardDocs/Simbli could provide school board member names.
items.notes: Extracted local candidate data from Civera ElectionStats GraphQL API for all 3 pilot jurisdictions. Fixed extraction pipeline: skip empty elections, namespace election IDs by jurisdiction, broadened division filters to capture council districts. San Rafael: 21 contests/37 candidates (mayor, council D1-D4, clerk, measures). Mill Valley: 8 contests/26 candidates. San Anselmo: 11 contests/29 candidates. School districts deferred (cross-city boundary mapping needed).

items.name: ballot_measure_content
items.description: Ingest ballot measure text, fiscal impact summaries, and pro/con arguments. State measures come from the CA voter guide (voterguide.sos.ca.gov). Local measures come from county sample ballots. Currently we only store pass/fail results, not the measure content itself.
items.time_sensitive: 2026-06-02 CA primary — measures on the ballot need explanatory content
items.notes: Model extended with full_text, fiscal_impact fields. to_dict() serializes all content fields. CA voter guide client extracts from LAO (fiscal impact) and VIG (full text, pro/con args). Civera extraction includes content field placeholders. Explore my_ballot displays ballot_measure data for measure-type contests. VIG HTML blocked by Cloudflare; LAO is accessible. VIG HTML for 2026 primary available April 3, 2026.

items.name: election_deadlines_scraping
items.description: Scrape key election deadlines from CA SOS: voter registration deadline (15 days before), same-day registration availability, mail ballot send date, early voting start, ballot drop-off locations. Currently election_deadlines table exists but is unpopulated.
items.time_sensitive: 2026-06-02 CA primary — registration deadline ~2026-05-18, deadlines must be surfaceable before then
items.notes: Implemented via generate_ca_deadlines() — computes standard CA deadlines (VBM mailing, registration, early voting, conditional registration, election day) from Elections Code rules. Seeded for all pilot jurisdictions. Deadlines now appear in whats_next() responses. Completed as part of election_calendar session.
